title: What the Superb Bird of Paradise shows

is_this_you.pressure: When it matters, you go dark around the one thing worth seeing, so nobody can look anywhere else.
is_this_you.love: You sweep the log for weeks before you dance. When the cape opens, it opens for one person, up close.
is_this_you.cost: You would rather keep rehearsing than show the dance half learned, and some seasons the visitor stops waiting.

opener.text: Beat one: the lights go down. The male's display feathers are a black so deep they reflect as little as 0.05 percent of the light hitting them head-on [s8] [s9]. McCoy and colleagues called it “an evolved optical illusion, which makes adjacent colours appear even brighter” [s8]. Beat two: the blue-green breast shield comes up beside it [s11]. You were born a Taurus in a Rooster year. You have always known how to set a stage.

tabs.label: Your stage
tabs.intro: Earth that waits. Metal that shines.

rows.text: Taurus is fixed Earth, ruled by Venus, the sign of the senses and slow work toward a clear reward [s1] [s2]. The Rooster is yin Metal, confident and frank, the bird that keeps time [s3] [s4] [s5]. Your patience is the ore. The Rooster in you polishes it, and then wants it seen.

The male dances on a fallen log in the understory, and he tosses the leaves off it first [s10] [s12]. Scientists still cannot say whether the sweeping is cleaning or part of the show [s10]. You could tell them. The getting ready is the show.

At the peak, the cape opens into a flat black oval with the blue shield set forward, likened to a bouncing smiling face [s10]. He bounces around the female in quick, shuffling hops [s10] [s11]. From outside, it looks like joy. From inside, you are counting every step.

tabs.label: The dark around you
tabs.intro: The black serves the bright thing.

rows.text: The bird's ordinary back feathers are a normal black, more reflective than the display plumage [s9]. Most of the year you wear the ordinary black too. People who think they know you have never seen the cape.

Taurus can be stubborn and slow to change, and the Rooster likes to be listened to [s1] [s5]. Together they can keep a rehearsal running for years. Show it before it is perfect. Someone has already come to the log.
Lighting, exhibition design, colour grading and tailoring all pay for one bright thing set against careful dark.

tabs.label: Who you dance for
tabs.intro: Three who stay for the whole act. One who walks out.
tabs.love_lead: In love you show almost nothing for months, then everything, face to face. Venus rules your sign [s1], and the Rooster is loyal once it chooses [s5]. You need someone who comes back to the log more than once. Three of the old pairings stay to the end.

easy.why: The Galápagos Tortoise (Taurus, Dragon year) is your secret friend, the Dragon being the Rooster's hidden ally, and it shares your sign [s3].
The Shoebill (Capricorn, Ox year) shares your trine of Ox, Snake and Rooster, and Capricorn is Earth like you [s3] [s1].
The Narwhal (Pisces, Ox year) is trine kin as well, bringing Pisces Water to soften your Earth [s3].

hard.why: The one who walks out is the Pallas's Cat (Scorpio, Rabbit year): the Rabbit clashes with the Rooster, and Scorpio sits opposite Taurus [s3] [s1].

story.text: In the New Guinea Highlands, bird-of-paradise plumes were wealth, though the sources do not name the superb species [s13] [s14]. Gimi men gave them in bridal and funeral payments [s14]. In the Wahgi Valley, Marie Reay recorded feathers as central to bride-price [s15]. There, a display could help pay for a marriage.

closing: Open the cape. Hold it one beat longer than feels safe. That hush is the forest, about to clap.
